Adjusted assessment: The FOMC kept the target range at 1.50–1.75% and characterized the economy as growing at a moderate pace with a strong labor market and sub-2% inflation, while continuing bill purchases and repo operations for implementation (not additional easing). Beige Book and SLOOS-style reports point to tighter private credit conditions: banks tightened standards and other terms for C&I and construction/land development loans, raised credit score thresholds and tightened credit limits, reported weaker loan demand in construction/land development and parts of consumer credit, and anticipate further tightening with some deterioration in collateral values. These developments add a headwind to growth and inflation, reinforcing a patient/no-tightening stance and nudging the tone more dovish than the base read, without signaling imminent easing.
